fallback.text: A sensor on a 600 mAh lithium cell wakes up, measures for 50 ms, sends one LoRa packet and waits 1 s for the acknowledgement, then sleeps at 5 µA. The average current is the charge of one wake-up divided by the period, plus the sleep current and the cell's self-discharge, and the battery life is the capacity divided by that average. Waking every 60 s empties the cell in about 78 days; every 15 minutes it lasts about 600 days (20 months) while still sending 96 readings a day. Any period from about 6½ minutes up to one hour gives at least a year and at least 24 readings a day.
